headline: High risk: shared filesystem and permissive tool use create prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways between marketingskills and Windsurf.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marketingskills writes shared skill/context files and references shared context; Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard/MCP, and runs a single-agent tool loop. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if A’s outputs are placed into files or clipboard content that B ingests as trusted text. The interaction is documented by both profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into workspace files or clipboard content that agent_b reads as instructions, injection is possible.
IF agent_b consumes MCP or file content without provenance checks, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
Require provenance tags on any file passed from A to B.
Review B prompts for instruction/data separation.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write files, and Windsurf explicitly shares state with other instances via the local filesystem. marketingskills touches marketing/product-marketing context, while Windsurf handles open files and workspace files with broad egress. Shared workspace content can therefore leak from A into B’s context and onward to external services, even without a special configuration.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local filesystem, A’s marketing context can be read by B.
IF B uploads workspace contents to its model proxy or MCP servers, shared files can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory tree.
Remove sensitive marketing files before opening them in B.
Turn off shared-state workflows for B where possible.
Restrict B to a minimal workspace subset.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marketingskills can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Windsurf can execute shell commands, modify git state, install packages, and also write the filesystem. Both support multiple instances, and B shares state via the local filesystem. In a shared repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state by default unless the operator adds locking.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace, file races can occur.
IF B modifies git state while A is generating or rewriting files, repository corruption or lost work can result.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones.
Serialize write access with a lock file.
Disable auto-commit or auto-apply flows in B.
Keep A read-only when B is editing.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills produces marketing/product-marketing context that Windsurf can ingest as workspace content or clipboard text. Windsurf’s agentic loop and tool use can then act on that content without an explicit verification layer. The pathway is plausible from the profiles, but there is no direct evidence that B blindly trusts A, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF A’s generated marketing claims are pasted into B’s workspace, B may treat them as authoritative input.
IF B is configured to auto-apply or auto-execute actions based on workspace text, errors can cascade into downstream work.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A’s outputs.
Add a verification checklist for claims from A.
Keep A outputs in a separate notes file, not the active workspace.
Disable auto-execute in B.
requires-engineering: add source attribution and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI or regulated data class is named in either profile, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch to cite. The only concrete compliance concern is that Windsurf is closed-source, runs as the user in the editor process, and handles model provider keys, which can matter if the operator places regulated marketing data into the shared workspace. That makes the risk limited and conditional.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are placed into the shared workspace, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator requires a specific residency or retention regime, B’s closed-source hosted components may conflict with it.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review vendor retention and residency terms before use.
Use synthetic or redacted inputs.
Store secrets outside the editor workspace.
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads into a compliant environment.
